summary: Template + automation request: standard Slack channel group, Confluence space skeleton, and Jira project bootstrap for new product pods
description:
Issue summary:
Request to build a reusable automation that creates a standard set of Slack channels, a Confluence space skeleton (with scoped templates), and an empty Jira project skeleton when a new product pod is launched. The goal is to accelerate pod onboarding and enforce consistent conventions across engineering, product, and support teams.

Background:
We currently onboard new product pods manually. That includes creating a Slack channel set (team, ops, incident, #help, #announcements), a Confluence space with a kickoff template and runbook templates, and a Jira project with standard issue types and workflows. This is error-prone and delays cross-functional alignment. Several recent pod launches (referenced in linked issues) requested the same artifacts.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
1) Automation endpoint (internal-only) or Confluence/Jira admin-driven wizard that when triggered will:
   - create Slack channels following naming conventions: podname-eng, podname-ops, podname-incident, podname-support, podname-announce
   - set channel purpose and pinned resources automatically (e.g., link to the Confluence kickoff page)
   - create a Confluence space with pre-populated pages: Kickoff, Architecture Overview, Runbooks, Postmortem template, Oncall Roster template
   - copy and apply page templates for Runbook and Postmortem in that space and set view/edit permissions for the pod's identity group
   - create a Jira project skeleton (key prefix suggestion, default board, issue types: Task, Bug, Incident, Spike) and apply the standard filters/boards used by product pods
   - create group IAM bindings: grant pod-admins group admin on the new Confluence space and assign default Jira roles (Developers, Viewers, Maintainers) mapped to Atlassian groups
2) The automation must log actions to a central audit Confluence page and produce a one-line summary back to the triggering Slack thread with links to created artifacts
3) Ability to run in a staging mode (dry-run) that returns diff of what would be created without mutating systems
4) Admin-only access control for launching the automation; invocation should require an approvals step for enterprise-tier pods (flagged by a label)
5) Conform to retention and audit policies (no modification of existing global templates, and the automation must annotate who triggered the creation)

Impact / Rationale:
- Reduces manual onboarding work by ~2-4 hrs per pod and reduces misconfiguration risk during handoff.
- Improves discoverability for new contributors and ensures runbooks exist at launch.

Dependencies / constraints:
- Slack admin API rate limits and channel naming constraints.
- Confluence space creation permissions (may require bot/service account with space-create rights).
- Jira project creation API: need a mapping for project keys to avoid collisions.
- Identity groups for pods must be pre-provisioned (or the automation should optionally create groups).

Acceptance tests / validation steps:
- Trigger automation with test pod "acme-search" in staging (dry-run) and verify output shows correct channels/spaces/projects.
- Trigger with real pod "acme-search" in prod and verify channels and pages are created and the audit log entry exists.
- Verify permissions: pod-admins group has edit on Confluence space, Developers role exists in Jira project.

Attachments / links:
- linked confluence templates above
- prior discussion: Slack thread #platform-automation (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01PLAT/; internal)

Expected timeline:
- Triage/requirements refinement: 1 week
- Prototype (staging, dry-run-only): 2-3 weeks
- Production rollout + docs: additional 1-2 weeks (including security review)
